scope: Science-backed candidate indicators and common reference scenarios; no adopted operational limits or mission/equipment defaults

sources.role: Long-period solar visibility and terrain sky solid-angle definitions
sources.limitation: Static/long-period geometry is not a requested mission-window history or irradiance.

sources.citation: Phipps et al. (2021), Galactic Cosmic Ray Proton Radiation Dosage Near a Simple Lunar Crater
sources.role: Terrain obscures part of the incident sky; geometric exposure is a useful separate indicator
sources.limitation: We use solid angle divided by 4*pi, not their dose values. No secondary-particle transport, response, material shielding or human dose is inferred.

sources.citation: Dobynde and Guo (2024), Guidelines for radiation-safe human activities on the Moon
sources.role: Existing checked lunar shielding/solar reference scenarios
sources.limitation: Published study cases, not selected hardware or a site dose. Do not multiply whole-field reference doses by the geometric proxy.

sources.role: Solar UV is relevant to lunar photoemission and the near-surface environment
sources.limitation: Sun visibility supplies an opportunity proxy only, not spectrum, incident energy, biological exposure or material degradation.

sources.role: Charging depends on electron/ion plasma and photoemission parameters and solar geometry
sources.limitation: Ion records and mean illumination alone do not establish local potential or discharge risk.

sources.citation: Rhodes and Farrell (2019), Lunar polar plasma environment, NASA GSFC
sources.role: Dark plasma-poor polar terrain can have difficulty dissipating triboelectric charge
sources.limitation: Darkness is not a universal charging benefit; there is no monotonic plasma score or invented voltage.

sources.citation: NASA-STD-7009B, Standard for Models and Simulations
sources.role: Document model assumptions, scope and credibility
sources.limitation: This prototype does not claim NASA-standard compliance or validated operational adequacy.

comparison_views.meaning: Pareto tradeoff among candidates passing the current illustrative filters. Lower geometric exposure/opportunity and higher Earth visibility; not an operational safety ranking.
comparison_views.solar_handling: Solar visibility remains an existing hard context filter, and is not also added as an independent weighted benefit in this view.

comparison_views.meaning: Same tradeoff with explicitly chosen lower phase-median span, only when complete fixed-common thermal cohorts exist. Not equipment-temperature adequacy.
comparison_views.solar_handling: No double-counted sunlight/UV weights; unsupported thermal candidates remain unranked in this view.
